summary_en.motivation: To investigate the microstructure evolution and defect formation mechanisms of a novel Al-Cu-Si-Sc-Zr alloy processed by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Samples were fabricated by SLM under varying process parameters, followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical property evaluation.
summary_en.result: Optimal parameters yielded nearly fully dense parts with refined grains and enhanced mechanical properties due to Sc and Zr addition.
summary_en.validation: Microstructure and mechanical performance were validated via SEM, EDS, XRD, and tensile/compression tests.

papers.title: High-Resolution Novel Indirect Bioprinting of Low-Viscosity Cell-Laden Hydrogels via Model-Support Bioink Interaction
papers.abstract: Bioprinting of unmodified soft extracellular matrix into complex 3D structures has remained challenging to fabricate. Herein, we established a novel process for the printing of low-viscosity hydrogel by using a unique support technique to retain the structural integrity of the support structure. We demonstrated that this process of printing could be used for different types of hydrogel, ranging from fast crosslinking gelatin methacrylate to slow crosslinking collagen type I. In addition, we evaluated the biocompatibility of the process by observing the effects of the cytotoxicity of L929 and the functionality of the human umbilical vein endothelium primary cells after printing. The results show that the bioprinted construct provided excellent biocompatibility as well as supported cell growth and differentiation. Thus, this is a novel technique that can be potentially used to enhance the resolution of the extrusion-based bioprinter.

papers.title: Hydroxyapatite Formation on Coated Titanium Implants Submerged in Simulated Body Fluid.
papers.abstract: Titanium implants are commonly used in the field of dentistry for prosthetics such as crowns, bridges, and dentures. For successful therapy, an implant must bind to the surrounding bone in a process known as osseointegration. The objective for this ongoing study is to determine the potential of different implant surface coatings in providing the formation of hydroxyapatite (HA). The coatings include titanium nitride (TiN), silicon dioxide (SiO2), and quaternized titanium nitride (QTiN). The controls were a sodium hydroxide treated group, which functioned as a positive control, and an uncoated titanium group. Each coated disc was submerged in simulated body fluid (SBF), replenished every 48 h, over a period of 28 days. Each coating successfully developed a layer of HA, which was calculated through mass comparisons and observed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive analysis x-rays (EDX). Among these coatings, the quaternized titanium nitride coating seemed to have a better yield of HA. Further studies to expand the data concerning this experiment are underway.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), stress shielding analysis, or porous structure design for stiffness matching.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估不同涂层促进钛植入物羟基磷灰石形成的能力。
summary_zh.method: 将TiN、SiO2、QTiN涂层钛片浸泡在模拟体液中28天。
summary_zh.result: 所有涂层均形成羟基磷灰石，QTiN效果最佳。
summary_zh.validation: 通过质量测量、SEM和EDX分析验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the potential of different surface coatings on titanium implants to promote hydroxyapatite formation for enhanced osseointegration.
summary_en.method: Coated titanium discs (TiN, SiO2, QTiN) were immersed in simulated body fluid for 28 days with replenishment every 48 hours.
summary_en.result: All coatings developed a hydroxyapatite layer, with quaternized titanium nitride showing the highest yield.
summary_en.validation: Hydroxyapatite formation was confirmed via mass measurements, SEM observation, and EDX analysis.
